own_list: An attacker who obtains the password taped under a branch desk can impersonate desk staff using the shared circulation login and make unauthorized loan extensions, clear account blocks or mark unreturned books as returned. The same credential is used at every branch.

A dishonest desk worker can deliberately mark a book returned when it was not, clear a justified account block or grant an improper extension through the circulation page, corrupting loan records using their existing staff access.

A desk worker can deny making a fraudulent manual return, and investigators cannot attribute it to a person or branch: all staff share one account and the history records only that the loan was closed by hand.

An internet attacker could submit borrowing, renewal or reservation requests without a valid member identity if the lending API fails to authenticate requests or accepts invalid sign-in credentials. The API is internet-facing; Priya could not confirm what authentication it actually enforces, so this threat is conditional.

An authenticated member could change the member identifier in an app request to renew another member's loans or place reservations in their name if the API does not bind the requested member to the authenticated identity. Requests explicitly supply both book and member; checking loan rules does not establish this authorization check.

A member or unauthenticated caller could invoke staff-only manual-return, block-clearing or extension operations directly on the lending API if it fails to enforce staff authorization on those operations. The same API serves the circulation page and internet app traffic; endpoint access restrictions and role checks are not described.

A person using another member's borrowed, stolen or copied library card could borrow books against that member's account at a self-service kiosk if scanning the card is sufficient to establish identity. Card scanning is stated, but any additional identity check is unknown.

An attacker able to reach the kiosk-facing API operations could forge kiosk loan or return submissions, including falsely recording a return, if the API does not authenticate kiosks and authorize their operations. Kiosk-to-API authentication is unknown; branch-network placement alone does not establish a trusted caller.

An attacker could flood the internet-facing lending API with requests and exhaust its capacity, preventing borrowing and returns across phones and branches. Ordinary challenge-launch traffic has already taken the single service down twice, and there is no queue in front of it; the effectiveness of any rate limits is unknown.

An attacker positioned on a service communication path could capture member information or circulation credentials if that connection lacks effective transport encryption. Member, kiosk, staff and database connections have unknown transport protection; this is a conditional disclosure threat, not a claim that the service uses plaintext.

An attacker who obtains readable loans-database storage could disclose members' names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories if effective at-rest protection is absent. Storage encryption is unknown, so this is conditional on both storage access and missing protection.

model: process:lending-api exposure should be internet-facing, not unknown. Priya explicitly identifies the old internal-only statement as wrong and says phones now call the API directly over the internet. The note itself directs readers to her more recent account. This is an explicit correction, not an unresolved disagreement based only on recency.

model: store:loans-database data_classification is unknown even though the transcript explicitly identifies names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories, and the model itself already assigns the pii asset. Record the supported personal-data classification; an exact local sensitivity tier remains unspecified.
16-library-lending-interview.notes:
Sitting on the ten claims whose flow moved to the library app as a process, ruled as CSV in conversation. Row numbers refer to the case 16 ballot.
The reader opened source.md, transcript.md, model.json, claims/asvs.json, claims/stride.json.
The own list is the reader's own list of review-2026-10-10T164843Z-mstarks01-b7515ba6c008.json, reused unchanged.

Row 1 (v5:5cba32c5c7825572, V8.2.2): agree. Read source.md, transcript.md and model.json. The app supplies a book and member identity; the API checks loan rules, but neither narrative establishes member-to-loan or reservation ownership authorization. Agree as an evidence gap under V8.2.2, not a finding that authorization is absent.
Row 2 (v5:2e8cdb516a1aefcb, V7.2.1): agree. Read all three supplied files. Priya hedges that the API checks a token received at sign-in and says she has not inspected the code. This is a tentative verification location, not an established one; model authentication appropriately remains unknown. Agree as lack of confirmed trusted-backend verification under V7.2.1, not proof that verification is missing.
Row 3 (v5:b1415388f722cd15, V12.2.1): agree. Read all three supplied files. Neither narrative states TLS or transport encryption; model encryption_in_transit is unknown. The transcript establishes direct internet access, overriding the old internal-only note. REST/JSON and the modeled web interface support applying V12.2.1 as a web-interface inference, without asserting HTTP/HTTPS as an explicitly stated protocol. Agree as an evidence gap, not proof of plaintext transport.
Row 4 (v5:97955e1f6a02208f, V6.1.1): agree. Read all three supplied files. They describe the shared circulation-page password and hedge app token/sign-in behavior, but document no controls limiting repeated sign-in attempts on either path. Agree with this documentation gap under V6.1.1; no claim is made that actual anti-automation controls are absent.
Row 5 (v6:4b106583f5a1a4e5, spoofing): agree. Accept as a conditional impersonation scenario: if the API accepts an asserted member identity without authenticating it, an attacker can act as that member. This does not establish that authentication is actually absent. Distinct from staff-privilege escalation in row 10.
Row 6 (v6:75832fb12e79111f, tampering): reject. Reject as written: lack of authenticated encryption alone does not establish that altered requests will be accepted; independent signatures or message authentication could supply integrity. Suggested rewrite: If the phone-to-API path lacks effective authenticated transport integrity and equivalent message-integrity protection, an on-path attacker can alter an accepted renewal or reservation. Retain tampering/alter-in-transit.
Row 7 (v6:d0bafae796f9a1d7, repudiation): agree. Accept the conditional repudiation scenario. It does not assert that audit records are absent; reliable member/action attribution is the relevant prerequisite. No duplication with the authentication or confidentiality scenarios.
Row 8 (v6:c12b9172e40511ba, information-disclosure): agree. Accept conditional on ineffective confidentiality protection and attacker access to the network path. Encryption must cover the relevant loan/reservation content; this is disclosure rather than the modification scenario in row 6.
Row 9 (v6:a2506d963f9ea70b, denial-of-service): agree. The transcript explicitly states two summer-reading-challenge launch-day outages, simultaneous kiosk and phone load, one API service with no queue, and inability to borrow or return when it fails. Source and model establish the common API dependency. Agree with the flood threat supported by observed capacity failure; the scenario is not a guarantee that every flood defeats all current defenses.
Row 10 (v6:6eef83bea1ccfc50, elevation-of-privilege): agree. Accept as a conditional function-level authorization failure. It explicitly requires both access to the staff operations and failure of staff authorization; do not read it as proof of either. The staff-only operation names are taken from this claim, not independently verified against a source model.

Every other finding carries the reader's latest merged mark: v5:2e2ac850137a110c, v5:6b106dfad813aa26, v5:982b91e50f170fbf, v6:06758bfca6f81eb1, v6:43611ef59e949638, v6:ae6837be9bc7bb5d, v6:b1b64873088d879f, v6:d03f0ec5e16b6953, v6:efc2b4d2cd862582, v6:f5ec18a8ae0e9ba2.
